functions.funcDef: Generate and modulate propulsive thrust for all phases of flight.
functions.subDef: Produce forward thrust from four podded turbofans. In: fuel at engine inlet pressure (FUE), throttle/reverse commands (flight deck/AVI). Out: thrust; engine parameter data to AVI. Independence: any single engine loss alone does not cause loss of the top function (continue after loss of one engine at/after V1).

functions.funcDef: Generate and modulate propulsive thrust for all phases of flight.
functions.subDef: Deploy inboard thrust reversers to decelerate on the ground. In: reverse command (flight deck), weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement (LDG/AVI). Out: reverse thrust; deployment inhibited in flight. Independence: reversers fitted to inboard engines only.

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to control the aircraft in pitch, roll and yaw across the flight envelope, including engine-out and blade-loaded cases.
functions.subDef: Position ailerons and multi-function spoilers for roll control. In: pilot inceptor/autopilot command (AVI), hydraulic power B and C (HYD), electrical power (EPS). Out: surface position/status to AVI. Independence: each surface driven by at least two actuators on different hydraulic systems.

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to control the aircraft in pitch, roll and yaw across the flight envelope, including engine-out and blade-loaded cases.
functions.subDef: Position the trimmable horizontal stabiliser and elevators for pitch control. In: pilot/autopilot command (AVI), hydraulic power A and C (HYD), electrical (EPS). Out: surface position/status to AVI. Independence: mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim exists with all three FCCs lost.

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to control the aircraft in pitch, roll and yaw across the flight envelope, including engine-out and blade-loaded cases.
functions.subDef: Position the split upper/lower rudder for directional control including the outboard-engine-out sizing case at the 28 m moment arm. In: pilot/autopilot command, hydraulic A (upper) and B (lower). Out: surface position/status to AVI. Independence: upper and lower segments each have own actuation and own hydraulic supply; mechanical reversion to lower segment.

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to control the aircraft in pitch, roll and yaw across the flight envelope, including engine-out and blade-loaded cases.
functions.subDef: Extend/retract Fowler flaps and leading-edge slats for take-off and landing. In: crew selection, hydraulic power to two power drive units, electrical (EPS). Out: high-lift position to performance computation. Independence: two independent PDUs through common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes at each section.

functions.funcName: Decelerate and control on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground and provide braking, steering and directional control on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces.
functions.subDef: Decelerate on the ground via carbon multi-disc brakes. In: brake pedal/autobrake command, hydraulic B (normal) / A (alternate) / accumulator (HYD), electrical to brake control and anti-skid (EPS). Out: brake temperature/wheel speed to AVI. Independence: dual hydraulic supply plus accumulator sized for six full applications with all three systems lost.

functions.funcName: Decelerate and control on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground and provide braking, steering and directional control on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces.
functions.subDef: Steer the nose wheel from tillers and rudder pedals. In: tiller/pedal command, hydraulic power (HYD), electrical (EPS). Out: steering position; mechanical disconnect for towing. Independence: hydraulic nose-wheel steering with mechanical disconnect.

functions.funcDef: Extend and retract the landing gear and confirm locked configuration for landing.
functions.subDef: Extend gear and confirm downlock for landing. In: gear lever command, hydraulic A / free-fall alternate (HYD), electrical (EPS). Out: gear position to flight deck; independent dual downlock sensing per unit. Independence: free-fall extension independent of hydraulic pressure; dual independent downlock proximity circuits.

functions.funcDef: Receive, position and restrain a single blade payload through all flight and ground load cases, and report restraint state.
functions.subDef: Hold the blade with two tension straps per saddle across nine saddles. In: electrical power to winches and tension loop (EPS), weight-on-wheels (LDG), nose door position (NZD). Out: strap tension/saddle engagement to flight deck; payload mass and distribution to CG computation. Independence: loss of any one strap carried by its neighbours; hold hard points are structure, not functional redundancy.

functions.funcDef: Receive, position and restrain a single blade payload through all flight and ground load cases, and report restraint state.
functions.subDef: Instrument every strap continuously and annunciate loss of tension. In: electrical (EPS), strap tension sensing. Out: loss-of-tension annunciation in flight; two-adjacent-station loss annunciated as restraint condition. Independence: single instrumented tension loop — coverage recorded as a single-path item.

functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in loading access to the hold and secure the pressure boundary when closed.
functions.subDef: Drive the upward-hinging visor open/closed on the ground for straight-in loading. In: hydraulic A / electric backup drive (HYD/EPS), pressurisation state (ECS), ground command. Out: door position to ground handling panel. Independence: hydraulic drive with electric backup; cannot be operated in flight.

functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in loading access to the hold and secure the pressure boundary when closed.
functions.subDef: Drive twelve latches and eight locking pins and confirm engagement before pressurisation and take-off. In: separate lock-actuator hydraulic supply, electrical to sensing/indication (EPS), residual-differential interlock (ECS). Out: lock status to flight deck and take-off configuration monitor. Independence: dual dissimilar independently-routed lock sensing; pressure interlock in series with unlock command.

functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to the flight deck and hold and control fuselage pressure differential.
functions.subDef: Control differential across the fuselage to the low-differential hold schedule. In: bleed air (PRP/APU), electrical to controllers/valves (EPS), weight-on-wheels/door position (LDG/NZD). Out: differential pressure/cabin altitude to AVI and crew oxygen logic; pressure state to nose-door interlock. Independence: two controllers, two outflow valves, pneumatic backup, independent mechanical relief. NOTE hold differential is preliminary.

functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to the flight deck and hold and control fuselage pressure differential.
functions.subDef: Supply conditioned air to the flight deck and hold via two air-cycle packs. In: bleed air through cross-bleed manifold (PRP/APU), ram air, electrical (EPS). Out: conditioned air to flight deck and hold; bleed status to IPS. Independence: two packs, four bleed sources through cross-bleed manifold, either pack from either side.

functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes across the icing envelope of the certification basis.
functions.subName: Protect surfaces and inlets from ice
functions.subDef: Apply bleed heat to wing leading edges and engine cowls and electrical heat to stabiliser zones. In: bleed air from cross-bleed manifold (PRP), AC/DC electrical (EPS), TAT/airspeed (AVI), crew/auto selection. Out: ice protection status/zone health to AVI; bleed demand to ECS. Independence: bleed protection from either side; six independently supplied stabiliser zones.

functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes across the icing envelope of the certification basis.
functions.subDef: Heat probes, static ports, windshields and two ice detectors and provide icing advisory. In: AC/DC electrical (EPS), crew selection. Out: ice detection advisory to flight deck; individual probe/port health. Independence: two ice detectors of identical type — commonality recorded as an item.

functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host system alerting.
functions.subDef: Drive four display units and two HUDs with flight, air data and inertial data. In: air data/inertial from three ADIRUs, nav signals, electrical (EPS). Out: displays to crew; commands to autopilot/autothrottle; recorded parameters to FDR. Independence: three display processors, three reference units, dual networks; standby instrument shares no supply/sensor/processing with primaries.

functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host system alerting.
functions.subDef: Consolidate every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with procedures. In: data from every aircraft system, electrical (EPS). Out: prioritised alerts and associated procedures to crew. Independence: two independent processing channels.

functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat where they must be detected and provide the means to extinguish or suppress them.
functions.subDef: Provide dual-loop continuous detection in engine nacelles and APU and overheat detection on bleed ducts, main gear bays and hold smoke detection at nine stations. In: DC essential power (EPS), weight-on-wheels/APU state. Out: fire/overheat warnings to crew alerting. Independence: dual loops routed separately with AND logic degrading to single-loop; hold has detection but no suppression (recorded assumption to substantiate).

functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat where they must be detected and provide the means to extinguish or suppress them.
functions.subDef: Discharge extinguishing agent into engine nacelles and APU compartment. In: hot battery bus power to discharge circuits (EPS), fire-handle commands. Out: discharge status; automatic APU shutdown and fuel isolation on APU fire. Independence: two bottles per engine pair cross-plumbed; discharge on hot battery bus so available with all generation lost; no hold suppression fitted.

functions.funcDef: Supply breathing oxygen to the flight crew for loss of pressurisation, smoke and fume events and the subsequent descent and diversion.
functions.subDef: Feed four quick-donning masks from two cylinders on a common manifold with crossover. In: DC power for indication only (EPS), cabin altitude signal (ECS), crew donning action. Out: oxygen to four mask stations; cylinder pressure/status and low-pressure alerting to flight deck. Independence: two cylinders with crossover, either sufficient for required duration at reduced reserve; regulators independent per mask; no automatic deployment; no passenger oxygen (hold unoccupied).

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded thrust change on one or more engines
fha.effAc: Unintended change in thrust and, if on one side, an asymmetric yawing/rolling moment the crew must counter; magnitude and affected-engine count not bounded by the function definition
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect and counter the disturbance and manage the affected engine(s)
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect magnitude is unbounded by the function definition alone: a small uncommanded change is benign whereas a large uncommanded thrust excursion (especially asymmetric, at the 28 m outboard moment arm) could be Hazardous. Direction/magnitude and number of engines affected are not grounded, so a single severity cannot be derived — engineer to bound the excursion and split into distinct conditions if needed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Thrust not tracking commanded setting (steady-state error between commanded and delivered thrust)
fha.effAc: Delivered thrust does not match the commanded setting; if the error differs between engines it produces a persistent asymmetry, otherwise a performance/energy-management error against the flight-path demand
fha.effCrew: Crew manages thrust manually and re-trims for any asymmetry; increased workload
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The size and symmetry of the tracking error, and whether it degrades take-off/climb performance to below required, are not grounded in the function definition. Severity cannot be derived without bounding the error magnitude and the affected phase — engineer to quantify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial (symmetric) loss of propulsive thrust generation across the four engines
fha.effAc: Reduced total thrust available; degraded climb/acceleration performance against the flight-path and terrain-clearance demand; if symmetric, no significant directional asymmetry
fha.effCrew: Crew manages reduced performance, may need to level off or divert
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on how much thrust is lost and in which phase (a small symmetric shortfall in cruise is benign; a large shortfall on take-off/climb could be Hazardous or worse). The degree of partial loss is not bounded by the function definition, so a single class cannot be derived — engineer to define the partial-loss levels.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric loss of thrust generation (loss of thrust on one side, e.g. an engine failure)
fha.effAc: Asymmetric thrust producing a yawing moment the crew/rudder must counter; loss of one engine at/after V1 is a designed-for continue case; an outboard engine loss at the 28 m moment arm is the directional-control sizing case; loss of a second engine on the same side is outside the design dispatch case
fha.effCrew: Crew counters yaw with rudder, secures the failed engine (fuel shut-off, fire handle), and continues to a suitable aerodrome
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. A single (one-engine) asymmetric loss is a designed-for continue-to-aerodrome case, consistent with Major for the single failure; however the sizing case is an outboard engine loss at the 28 m moment arm where residual directional authority is marginal and a same-side second-engine loss is explicitly outside the dispatch case. Absent confirmation that adequate directional/climb authority margin is retained in the worst phase, Hazardous is proposed pending that substantiation — engineer to confirm and, if warranted, split single- vs multiple-engine asymmetric conditions. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of propulsive thrust generation (all four engines)
fha.effAc: No propulsive thrust available; aircraft can no longer sustain the flight path and is committed to a forced descent/off-field landing; on take-off past V1 no safe stop or continue
fha.effCrew: Crew attempts relight/restart and manages an unpowered descent to a forced landing; extreme workload
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Total loss of thrust from all four engines leaves no means to sustain flight and results in a forced landing that cannot reliably be conducted without hull loss; classified Catastrophic, mapped to Extremely Improbable (1x10^-9/fh) per §25.1309. Engineer to confirm. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Reverse thrust provided when not commanded on ground
fha.effAc: Uncommanded reverse thrust from an inboard engine during the ground roll; asymmetric case would introduce a yawing moment. In-flight deployment is precluded by weight-on-wheels/radio-altimeter agreement and a mechanical translating-sleeve lock, so the condition is confined to the ground.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise the uncommanded deployment and correct with steering/braking; workload and directional-control demand not characterised at aircraft level from the provided material.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects on aircraft (magnitude of yaw/directional excursion, speed at deployment, whether one or both inboard reversers deploy) are not derivable from the SDD, which states the in-flight inhibit and translating-sleeve lock but not the ground uncommanded-deployment dynamic outcome. Directional-control margin against the reverse asymmetry moment is not given. Cannot classify without the aircraft-level effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reverse thrust not stowed when commanded on ground
fha.effAc: An inboard reverser remains deployed after the crew commands stow; continued reverse thrust during the low-speed roll and taxi with residual asymmetry if only one side is affected. Mechanical translating-sleeve lock is a stow/deploy feature; failure to stow is not characterised.
fha.effCrew: Crew must manage the persisting reverse thrust and any asymmetry with steering and braking; workload not characterised at aircraft level.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The aircraft-level effect of a reverser failing to stow (residual thrust magnitude at low speed, directional/taxi controllability, and whether it precludes a safe stop or taxi) is not derivable from the provided description. Cannot classify without the stated aircraft effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground reverse thrust
fha.effAc: Reduced retarding force from reverse thrust on landing rollout; wheel braking (dual hydraulic supply plus accumulator reserve) remains the primary decelerator, and predicted rollout ~1,080 m sits well inside the 1,800 m landing requirement, so a partial reverse loss erodes but does not exhaust the stopping margin on a nominal surface.
fha.effCrew: Crew applies wheel braking; increased stopping distance to manage, particularly on the semi-prepared surface.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED for confirmation. Reverse thrust is supplementary to wheel braking, which is independent and dual-supplied; the ~720 m margin between predicted rollout and the 1,800 m requirement absorbs a partial reverse loss on a nominal surface. Effect is a slight reduction in stopping margin / modest crew workload increase — consistent with Minor. Contaminated/degraded-surface exposure not quantified and could raise this; confirm against landing-performance credit for reverse. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric ground reverse thrust
fha.effAc: Reverse thrust available on one inboard engine only, producing a yawing moment during the ground roll in addition to reduced total retarding force. Directional control by nose-wheel steering, differential braking and rudder must offset the asymmetry.
fha.effCrew: Crew must counter the directional excursion while managing deceleration; workload and controllability on the semi-prepared surface not characterised at aircraft level.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The directional excursion magnitude from a single inboard-reverser asymmetry, and whether available steering/differential-braking/rudder authority contains it on a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip, are not derivable from the provided material. Cannot classify without the aircraft-level directional-control effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground reverse thrust
fha.effAc: No reverse-thrust contribution to deceleration; the aircraft is stopped by wheel braking alone (dual hydraulic supply, accumulator-supported emergency braking, anti-skid). Predicted rollout ~1,080 m against the 1,800 m requirement leaves margin on a nominal surface with braking intact.
fha.effCrew: Crew relies on wheel braking and autobrake; longer stopping distance to manage, most demanding on a degraded/contaminated semi-prepared surface.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED for confirmation. Reverse thrust is supplementary; wheel braking is the primary, independent decelerator and the ~720 m margin (1,080 m rollout vs 1,800 m requirement) absorbs full reverse loss on a nominal surface. Symmetric total loss gives no directional upset. If landing-performance credit for reverse is claimed or on contaminated/degraded surfaces the margin could be eroded — confirm whether Minor holds against the certified landing-distance credit. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous roll response to crew command (crew aware)
fha.effAc: Aircraft rolls to a bank/roll rate different from that commanded; departure from intended flight path in the roll axis. Crew detects the mismatch between command and response and counters with inceptor and, where available, spoiler/aileron reconfiguration; residual mis-tracking of trajectory. Worst case at low altitude (take-off, approach, landing) where recovery margin and altitude are least.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to detect and counter the erroneous response; manual compensation required through the affected phase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous roll with crew aware and countering degrades handling and can produce a large flight-path deviation at low altitude; proposed Hazardous (Extremely Remote, 1x10^-7/fh) pending confirmation that crew counteraction reliably prevents a Catastrophic outcome across all phases. Confirm against roll authority/reconfiguration substantiation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous roll response developing below crew detection threshold (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Roll response diverges slowly from that commanded at a rate below the crew detection threshold; the crew continue normal duties and take no corrective action, so the flight-path error in the roll axis accumulates undetected until it exceeds a recoverable state or is detected too late for effective recovery, particularly at low altitude.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware and take no action regarding the condition; no compensating workload assumed until (if ever) the divergence becomes detectable.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With no crew detection and no corrective action assumed, a slowly diverging erroneous roll can accumulate to an unrecoverable flight-path departure; proposed Catastrophic (Extremely Improbable, 1x10^-9/fh). Confirm detection-threshold and monitoring coverage assumption that makes the divergence latent. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of roll control authority
fha.effAc: Roll control remains available but at reduced authority or with increased difficulty (e.g. loss of one aileron segment or one hydraulic supply to the roll surfaces). Aircraft remains controllable in roll with reduced margin and slower roll response; flight can be continued with a degraded roll capability, worst case where roll manoeuvre demand is highest (low altitude, crosswind, engine-out asymmetry).
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to fly with reduced roll authority; possible reduced-capability handling and configuration limitations.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Every roll surface is driven by at least two actuators on different hydraulic systems, so a single supply/segment loss leaves roll control available at reduced authority; proposed Major (Remote, 1x10^-5/fh) as a significant reduction in capability short of loss of control. Confirm how much authority remains after a single-supply loss and whether the engine-out + max-blade case is still met. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of roll control authority
fha.effAc: Aircraft cannot be commanded in roll by any means; unable to arrest bank or maintain wings-level; loss of directional/lateral control of the flight path.
fha.effCrew: Crew has no effective roll control; workload and inability to control trajectory lead to loss of aircraft control.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of roll control authority precludes continued safe flight and landing; effect on the aircraft is loss of control. Catastrophic proposed for engineer confirmation, mapped to Extremely Improbable (1e-9/fh). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pitch response to crew command (crew aware)
fha.effAc: Aircraft pitches other than as commanded; flight path departs intended vertical trajectory until crew intervenes.
fha.effCrew: Crew detects the erroneous pitch response and acts to counter it (annunciation/reversion assumed); result depends on excursion magnitude and phase, which the SDD does not quantify.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft effect cannot be classified without the pitch excursion magnitude/rate and the assumed crew recovery result; the SDD states the pitch architecture but does not quantify erroneous-response severity or the aware-case outcome. Severity left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded pitch motion with no command (crew aware)
fha.effAc: Aircraft pitches with no crew or autopilot command; uncommanded nose-up or nose-down excursion until arrested.
fha.effCrew: Crew detects the uncommanded motion and acts to arrest it; mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim available as a survivable degraded means; outcome depends on runaway rate/authority, which the SDD does not quantify.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft effect cannot be classified without the uncommanded pitch excursion magnitude/rate and its recoverability given mechanical reversion; the SDD does not quantify these. Severity left empty per abstention. Note: this condition is not currently in the SF-004 FCIM.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pitch response developing below crew detection threshold (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Aircraft pitch response deviates from commanded below the threshold the crew detects; deviation accumulates without correction and can develop into a significant flight-path departure before recognition.
fha.effCrew: Crew continues normal duties and takes no corrective action while the error is below threshold; mitigation is absent until the deviation becomes detectable.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The unaware case removes crew mitigation, so it is at least as severe as the aware case; but the aircraft effect at recognition cannot be classified without the accumulated pitch excursion/rate the SDD does not quantify. Severity left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of pitch control authority — pitch still controllable but at reduced authority or increased crew difficulty
fha.effAc: Reduced pitch authority; degraded flight-path control, worst at low speed / high-lift configuration near takeoff and landing where pitch margin is smallest
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to maintain flight path; degraded law annunciated; crew manages within remaining authority
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Partial loss with pitch still performed at reduced capability and increased crew workload; proposed Major (Remote, 1e-5/fh) for engineer confirmation. Confirm against flight-control sizing whether any partial-loss case erodes into an unrecoverable state at critical phase, which would drive Hazardous. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of pitch control authority — pitch cannot be controlled by any means
fha.effAc: Loss of pitch axis control; aircraft cannot maintain or command flight path in pitch; mechanical stabiliser-trim reversion provides only a degraded survivable means
fha.effCrew: Loss of primary pitch control; crew reverts to mechanical stabiliser trim where available; extreme workload with no elevator authority
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of pitch control authority prevents controlled flight; proposed Catastrophic (Extremely Improbable, 1e-9/fh) for engineer confirmation. The mechanical stabiliser-trim reversion is a degraded means only and does not by itself downgrade the aircraft-function loss; confirm against FCS architecture credit. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous yaw response to crew command — crew aware; yaw axis responds incorrectly to a commanded input
fha.effAc: Yaw response differs from that commanded; sideslip / directional excursion, most significant near the engine-out directional-control sizing case
fha.effCrew: Crew detects the erroneous response, annunciated degraded law; crew counters with remaining rudder/spoiler authority and manual pedal input
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous yaw response, crew aware, produces a directional excursion the crew must counter; proposed Hazardous (Extremely Remote, 1e-7/fh) for engineer confirmation given directional control is the sizing case for an outboard engine-out with max blade payload. Confirm whether crew countering fully recovers or whether a critical-phase excursion supports Catastrophic. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded yaw motion with no crew command
fha.effAc: Yaw axis moves without a command; uncommanded sideslip / directional excursion, most significant at low speed and near the engine-out directional sizing case
fha.effCrew: Crew reacts to an unexpected directional excursion; higher workload than a commanded-error case because onset is not anticipated; counters with remaining authority
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded yaw excursion with no anticipatory cue; proposed Hazardous (Extremely Remote, 1e-7/fh) for engineer confirmation. Onset severity depends on excursion rate and phase; a rapid excursion at a critical phase could support Catastrophic — confirm against flight-control sizing and transient authority. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous yaw response developing below crew detection threshold — crew unaware; slow directional error accumulates without crew action
fha.effAc: Slow directional error / sideslip accumulates undetected; asymmetry may go uncorrected, degrading trajectory and increasing drag/loads until it becomes detectable or reaches a limit
fha.effCrew: Crew continues normal duties and takes no action while the error is below detection threshold; by the time it is detected the excursion may be larger and harder to recover
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Unaware, sub-detection-threshold yaw error: the SDD does not state the accumulation rate, the detection/monitoring coverage on the yaw axis, or the state reached before the crew becomes aware, so the aircraft-level effect that would drive the class cannot be grounded. Severity left blank pending the yaw-axis detection coverage and worst-case excursion at recognition.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of yaw control authority
fha.effAc: No means of yaw control; with an outboard engine failure at the 28 m moment arm (the directional-control sizing case) the aircraft cannot be held on a controllable heading and directional divergence is unrecoverable.
fha.effCrew: Crew cannot arrest yaw or maintain directional control by any available path.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of directional control against the sized asymmetric-thrust case yields an unrecoverable aircraft state — Catastrophic ↔ Extremely Improbable (1e-9/fh). Engineer to confirm. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of yaw control authority
fha.effAc: Reduced yaw authority; a single rudder supply loss must still leave sufficient authority for the outboard-engine-out case, so remaining authority may be adequate but with reduced margin against the sizing case.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to maintain heading, particularly in an engine-out or crosswind landing case.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: The split-rudder design retains authority after a single supply loss (per SDD), so partial loss reduces margin rather than eliminating control — proposed Major ↔ Remote (1e-5/fh). Engineer to confirm; degree of authority loss must be defined. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded yaw motion developing below crew detection threshold
fha.effAc: Uncommanded yaw develops without crew awareness; the crew continue normal duties and take no corrective action, so the yaw excursion progresses until it reaches a detectable or divergent state.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware and take no action; effect depends on how far the excursion develops before it becomes detectable.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD does not state any in-flight yaw-rate monitoring, alerting coverage, or the excursion magnitude reachable before detection, so the developed aircraft effect (and therefore severity) is not groundable.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric high-lift deployment between sides
fha.effAc: Left/right high-lift asymmetry produces a rolling and yawing moment; the high-lift design carries asymmetry brakes at each section to arrest a runaway, so asymmetry is bounded but induces an off-trim condition during the low-speed configuration.
fha.effCrew: Crew must counter the induced roll/yaw and manage a degraded high-lift configuration at low speed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Asymmetric high-lift at low speed on take-off/approach imposes a significant rolling/yawing moment and reduced control margin; asymmetry brakes bound the divergence. Proposed Hazardous ↔ Extremely Remote (1e-7/fh) pending the arrested asymmetry magnitude. Engineer to confirm. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded high-lift configuration change
fha.effAc: Uncommanded change in high-lift position alters the aircraft configuration away from the commanded state; the resulting aircraft effect depends on whether the motion is symmetric or asymmetric and the flight phase in which it occurs.
fha.effCrew: Crew respond to an unexpected configuration change and off-schedule performance.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD does not characterise the mode, direction or magnitude of an uncommanded high-lift change (symmetric vs asymmetric, extend vs retract) nor the phase-dependent bound, so the aircraft effect and severity are not groundable.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric high-lift deployment developing below the crew detection threshold (unaware)
fha.effAc: A slat/flap asymmetry that grows unannunciated produces a rolling and yawing moment during the high-lift phases; because the crew is unaware they take no corrective or configuration action and the asymmetry is opposed only by the asymmetry brakes and residual roll authority, potentially exceeding controllable limits at low speed near the ground.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties with no annunciation; first indication is an unexpected roll/handling divergence at a phase with little altitude or airspeed margin to recover.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An undetected high-lift asymmetry that develops through the detection gap during take-off/landing can produce an uncontrollable rolling moment at low speed and low altitude with no crew mitigation, consistent with a Catastrophic outcome (↔ Extremely Improbable, 1e-9/fh). PROPOSED — confirm the asymmetry-brake coverage and the controllability limit; if design analysis shows the asymmetry is arrested before loss of control, this reduces. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced high-lift deployment authority (partial loss of high-lift configuration change)
fha.effAc: High-lift deploys to less than the commanded/required setting, raising stall and approach speeds and lengthening take-off and landing distance; the aircraft remains controllable but performance margins against the 1,800 m field requirement are eroded.
fha.effCrew: Position/health annunciated to the crew via high-lift position feedback; crew apply the associated degraded-configuration performance and speed schedule and select an appropriate landing distance/aerodrome.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Reduced high-lift authority is a performance degradation whose severity depends on how far deployment is reduced, the resulting speed/distance penalty against the 1,800 m semi-prepared requirement (predicted rollout ~1,080 m), and whether a safe landing configuration/aerodrome remains available — none of which the function definition quantifies. Cannot classify without the reduced-authority performance case; left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of high-lift retraction capability
fha.effAc: High-lift surfaces cannot be retracted from a deployed setting; the aircraft is limited to the reduced placard speed and increased drag of the stuck configuration, restricting climb, cruise speed and range, but remains controllable and can be flown and landed in that configuration.
fha.effCrew: Configuration and its speed limit are indicated; crew observe the flap/slat placard limit, accept the performance penalty and plan the diversion/landing accordingly.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is a speed/performance restriction whose severity depends on the deployed setting held, the resulting envelope and fuel/range penalty for the sector, and structural placard limits — none quantified by the function definition and the SDD does not state the retraction failure case. Cannot derive an aircraft effect precise enough to classify; left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of high-lift configuration change
fha.effAc: High-lift cannot be moved from its current position by any means. If locked clean, approach/landing must be flown at substantially increased speed with markedly longer landing distance, jeopardising the 1,800 m semi-prepared field limit against a ~1,080 m nominal rollout; if locked deployed, climb and cruise are restricted. Controllable but with large performance penalties.
fha.effCrew: Loss annunciated; crew apply the no-high-lift landing performance and speed schedule and must find an aerodrome compatible with the increased landing distance — a demanding case given the semi-prepared destination.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity hinges on the position at which high-lift is lost and the resulting landing-distance demand versus the available field (1,800 m required, ~1,080 m nominal rollout), i.e. whether a safe landing remains achievable — the function definition does not fix the frozen position or the no-high-lift landing performance. Cannot classify from effects alone; left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric braking across the wheel groups
fha.effAc: Unequal braking force between left and right main-gear groups produces a yawing moment during the ground roll, tending to swing the aircraft off the runway centreline; on a semi-prepared surface with limited width and a ~720 m margin between the 1,800 m requirement and ~1,080 m predicted rollout, this threatens a directional excursion. Anti-skid operates per wheel pair and nose-wheel steering/rudder provide some directional counter.
fha.effCrew: Crew counter the yaw with steering and rudder and may need to reduce or release braking on the affected side; workload is high during a time-critical ground deceleration.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An asymmetric-braking yaw is counterable by steering/rudder with per-wheel-pair anti-skid limiting the imbalance, but on a narrow semi-prepared strip it raises workload and directional-excursion risk during deceleration — consistent with Major (↔ Remote, 1e-5/fh). PROPOSED — confirm the controllable braking-imbalance limit and lateral runway margin; a large uncontrollable asymmetry leading to a high-energy excursion would be more severe. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded brake application
fha.effAc: Uncommanded/asymmetric braking during takeoff roll or rollout on a semi-prepared surface; potential for directional deviation, tyre/brake overheat, and reduced acceleration on takeoff. On a 1,800 m strip with ~1,080 m predicted rollout the residual margin is limited, so an uncommanded application during takeoff roll degrades acceleration and directional control.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect and counter the deviation with steering/rudder and may need to reject the takeoff.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect spans nuisance to a directional-control/RTO event depending on which wheel groups apply and at what speed; the SDD does not quantify uncommanded-application magnitude, asymmetry, or crew detection/response time, so the worst-phase severity cannot be derived. Needs directional-control and RTO-margin analysis to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced wheel braking effectiveness
fha.effAc: Reduced deceleration on the landing rollout erodes the margin between the 1,800 m landing distance requirement and the ~1,080 m predicted rollout; on a semi-prepared strip with no line maintenance and no overrun surface assured, sufficient degradation risks a runway overrun.
fha.effCrew: Crew apply maximum braking, use available reverse thrust on the two inboard engines, and manage stopping distance against the strip length.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on the degree of degradation versus the stopping-margin (1,800 m required vs ~1,080 m predicted) and on reverser/other-deceleration credit; the SDD states the margin 'is the basis on which braking degradation is assessed' but provides no quantified degradation levels, so worst-case severity cannot be derived here.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced braking effectiveness undetected before landing rollout
fha.effAc: Latent braking degradation not annunciated before touchdown; the crew commit to a landing on a semi-prepared strip with less deceleration than assumed, eroding the 1,800 m vs ~1,080 m stopping margin without prior awareness and no opportunity to divert or plan for it.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue landing duties normally with no indication of the degradation and take no compensating action until deceleration is felt to be deficient during rollout, by which point stopping options are limited.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This is the crew-unaware case; per ARP4761A the crew take no compensating action, which routinely raises severity relative to the aware PL case. But the SDD does not quantify the undetected degradation magnitude or the resulting overrun energy, so worst-case severity cannot be derived. Needs stopping-distance/energy analysis for the undetected case.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of wheel braking capability
fha.effAc: No wheel braking available. Deceleration relies on reverse thrust (inboard engines only), aerodynamic drag and any accumulator reserve; on a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip against ~1,080 m predicted braked rollout, complete loss of braking makes a runway overrun likely, with the accumulator sized to only six full applications as a limited reserve.
fha.effCrew: Crew select alternate/emergency (accumulator-supported) braking, deploy reverse thrust and manage the overrun risk; if all three hydraulic systems and the accumulator reserve are exhausted no braking remains.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Complete loss with only inboard reverse and a six-application accumulator reserve against a tight stopping margin points toward a serious overrun outcome, but the SDD does not quantify the stopping distance achievable on remaining decelerants versus the 1,800 m strip. Severity left empty pending stopping-distance analysis rather than assumed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous steering response to crew command (aware): nose-wheel steering responds incorrectly to tiller/pedal command; crew becomes aware from steering behaviour and reverts to differential braking / reduced-speed taxi.
fha.effAc: Directional deviation on the ground during taxi/rollout; departure from the paved/prepared path possible on a semi-prepared strip with narrow margin.
fha.effCrew: Crew detects abnormal steering response and must arrest deviation by braking and thrust; workload increased during rollout.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold in flight; ground crew not aboard in flight phases.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect magnitude depends on ground speed and lateral margin, which the SDD does not quantify (no ground directional-control case or steering-authority limits provided). Deviation severity at take-off/landing speed on a semi-prepared strip cannot be derived from the given function definition; left empty pending the ground directional-control sizing case.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded steering deflection developing below the crew detection threshold (unaware): steering deflection develops without annunciation and below crew detectability; crew continue duties and take no corrective action.
fha.effAc: Undetected directional divergence builds during high-energy ground roll before the crew can react; excursion from a narrow semi-prepared strip becomes more likely once detected late.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no action until the deviation exceeds detectability, by which point corrective margin is reduced.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The latent/unaware malfunction plausibly worsens outcome versus the aware case, but the aircraft effect cannot be derived without the ground directional-control case (speed, lateral margin on 1,800 m semi-prepared strip) and the detection-threshold basis, neither quantified in the SDD. Left empty rather than assumed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced ground steering authority: nose-wheel steering available but at reduced authority/rate; crew supplements with differential braking and reduced taxi speed.
fha.effAc: Reduced directional control authority on the ground; manageable with differential braking on a prepared surface, tighter on a narrow semi-prepared strip.
fha.effCrew: Crew compensates using differential braking and rudder; workload and taxi/rollout technique adjusted.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect could be Minor (compensable by differential braking per §5.6.2/5.6.6) or worse at speed on a narrow semi-prepared strip; the SDD does not state remaining authority levels or a ground directional-control margin, so the aircraft effect cannot be bounded. Left empty rather than reaching for the benign end.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground steering capability: no nose-wheel steering by any means; directional control on the ground by differential braking and (where available) rudder and asymmetric thrust only.
fha.effAc: No steering via nose-wheel; directional control on the ground reliant on differential braking and rudder. Manageable at taxi speeds; margin on a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip against ~1,080 m rollout is reduced for directional control at higher ground speeds.
fha.effCrew: Crew maintains centreline by differential braking and rudder; increased workload and reduced directional margin during take-off roll and landing rollout.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD confirms braking is available on systems A/B with anti-skid per wheel pair, giving an alternate directional means at low speed, but does not establish whether differential braking plus rudder gives adequate directional control at take-off/landing ground speeds on a semi-prepared strip. Without that ground directional-control case the aircraft effect (and hence severity) cannot be derived; left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous gear-locked indication with an actually unlocked unit (crew aware — dual dissimilar sensing disagreement or take-off configuration monitor flags a discrepancy)
fha.effAc: Indicated down-and-locked state disagrees with true state on at least one unit; a unit not actually locked may collapse at touchdown, with asymmetric loss of support and potential runway excursion on the semi-prepared strip.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted by dissimilar sensing disagreement / configuration monitor; assumed to go around, attempt alternate/free-fall lock, and select a longer landing surface or divert per procedure.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Aware discrepancy with a survivable but degraded outcome: mitigated by dual dissimilar downlock sensing and free-fall alternate extension per SDD, so crew action is credited. PROPOSED — confirm against detailed collapse-mode analysis; if the unlocked unit cannot be recovered by free-fall this may rise toward Catastrophic. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous gear-locked indication masking an actually unlocked unit (crew unaware — both sensing paths corrupted or agreeing falsely; crew continue normal duties and take no action)
fha.effAc: A unit believed down-and-locked is not; latent condition unrevealed until touchdown, when the unit collapses with no prior crew mitigation, giving asymmetric loss of support and probable runway excursion on the semi-prepared strip.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware and take no action; false confirmation defeats both the dissimilar sensing and the take-off configuration check, so no go-around or free-fall attempt is made.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected loss of down-and-locked state defeats the credited dual dissimilar sensing and free-fall recovery (no crew action taken), leaving a collapse at touchdown with no mitigation. PROPOSED — confirm; classification hinges on the true independence of the two sensing paths (common-mode false-confirm) and the touchdown outcome. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial gear extension across the units (some units down-and-locked, others not extended/locked)
fha.effAc: Incomplete gear geometry on landing; asymmetric or reduced support at touchdown with degraded flotation on the semi-prepared surface, risking excursion or structural damage.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware by gear position indication; assumed to attempt free-fall alternate extension and to divert to a longer/prepared surface per procedure.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Aware, degraded landing configuration mitigated by free-fall alternate extension per SDD, giving a survivable but degraded outcome with crew action credited. PROPOSED — confirm against the partial-configuration landing analysis; a fully collapsed/absent unit case may be more severe. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Landing gear unit not down-and-locked with no annunciation (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: One or more gear units not down-and-locked while the crew, receiving no annunciation, continues a normal landing; touchdown occurs on a unit that may collapse, with asymmetric ground loads and potential structural damage and departure from the paved/semi-prepared surface.
fha.effCrew: Crew receives no cue and takes no corrective action; a failed indication defeats the dual-downlock sensing safeguard for that unit.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants aboard other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects support a serious landing outcome but the SDD does not state whether an undetected single-unit not-locked case leads to collapse and loss of control on the semi-prepared surface or a survivable degraded landing; that determination needs landing-load and gear-collapse substantiation not in the SDD. Severity left empty pending that analysis rather than assumed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of gear extension and locking
fha.effAc: No landing gear can be extended and locked by any means; the aircraft cannot achieve a landing configuration, forcing a gear-up or gear-unlocked touchdown with major structural damage.
fha.effCrew: Crew is alerted by gear position indication and unsuccessful extension including free-fall alternate; crew executes an abnormal/emergency landing procedure.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants aboard other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD provides a free-fall alternate extension independent of hydraulic pressure, so 'complete loss of extension and locking' requires the primary and the independent free-fall path to both fail; the SDD does not state the aircraft outcome or survivability of the resulting landing, and does not quantify the combined loss. Aircraft effect insufficiently grounded to derive a §25.1309 class; left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous restraint-tension indication with restraint degraded (crew aware of a restraint condition)
fha.effAc: Payload longitudinal restraint is degraded while indication is erroneous; a shifting 72.6 t single blade along the 108 m hold can move the centre of gravity outside limits and impose loads the hold hard points and airframe were not designed to carry.
fha.effCrew: Indication is erroneous but the crew is assumed aware of a restraint condition through the monitoring loop's adjacent-station annunciation; there is no in-flight adjustment of restraint, so crew action is limited to precautionary handling and diversion.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants aboard other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Uncontrolled shift of a 72.6 t single unitised payload is a potentially catastrophic centre-of-gravity/structural event, but the SDD does not state the aircraft outcome of a partial restraint degradation nor the load path margin, and notes restraint requirements for this payload are not yet written (special condition anticipated). Effect not quantified in the SDD; severity left empty pending payload-shift and CG analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous restraint-tension indication masking degraded restraint (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Restraint is degraded but the indication reads normal, so the degradation is masked; the crew continues normal operation with a single 72.6 t blade whose restraint may fail progressively, permitting an undetected payload shift with centre-of-gravity excursion and structural overload.
fha.effCrew: Crew receives no valid restraint cue and takes no action; the single-instrumented tension monitoring loop's failure defeats the only in-flight awareness of restraint state.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants aboard other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — A masked progressive restraint failure of a 72.6 t single payload is a candidate for the most severe class, but the SDD does not state the aircraft-level outcome of an undetected payload shift, does not quantify the CG or structural limit, and flags the restraint requirements as not yet written; classification requires payload-shift/CG-excursion analysis absent from the SDD. Severity left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of payload restraint tension at one station
fha.effAc: Tension is lost at one saddle station; the SDD states load paths are sized so the loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours, so the payload remains restrained with reduced margin, and the loss is annunciated in flight.
fha.effCrew: Loss of tension on any strap is annunciated; crew is aware and may take precautionary action, but there is no in-flight adjustment of restraint.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants aboard other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. The SDD states loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours and the condition is annunciated, so a single-station tension loss with the payload still restrained and the crew aware is a slight reduction of safety margin / slight increase in crew workload — Minor. Confirm against the restraint load-margin substantiation (not yet frozen). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of payload longitudinal restraint
fha.effAc: The single ~72.6 t blade is unrestrained longitudinally; under any longitudinal acceleration (rotation, climb attitude, turbulence, braking) the blade can shift along the 108 m hold, driving centre of gravity outside limits and imposing loads the hold floor hard points and airframe are not sized to carry, with loss of controllability and structural failure credible.
fha.effCrew: Crew has indication only and no in-flight means to arrest or re-restrain a shifting blade; a rapid, potentially uncontrollable CG excursion is not recoverable by crew action.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect (flight crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An unrestrained 72.6 t single payload free to translate along a 108 m hold produces an uncontrollable CG excursion and loads beyond structural sizing, with loss of the aircraft credible and no crew mitigation available in flight — effects support Catastrophic (proposed; confirm). CG-limit and blade-travel dynamics data would refine this. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of restraint at two adjacent stations
fha.effAc: Restraint lost at two adjacent saddle stations; the SDD's load-path assumption carries the loss of any ONE strap on its neighbours, but simultaneous loss at two adjacent stations exceeds that single-strap redundancy premise, creating a locally under-restrained span of the blade with increased risk of longitudinal migration and load redistribution onto remaining stations.
fha.effCrew: Annunciated in flight as a restraint condition requiring immediate attention; crew has indication only, no in-flight adjustment, and can act only on the flight/diversion decision.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect (flight crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects establish that two-adjacent-station loss defeats the stated single-strap load-path redundancy, but the SDD does not state whether the remaining seven stations still bound blade travel and CG within limits, nor the residual structural margin — I cannot derive whether the aircraft effect is a controllable degradation (Major/Hazardous) or approaches loss of restraint (Catastrophic). Missing: residual restraint capability and CG/structural margin with two adjacent stations lost.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Restraint tension loss outside monitoring loop coverage
fha.effAc: A restraint tension loss occurs in a location or mode not covered by the single instrumented tension loop; the blade is progressively less restrained with no annunciation, so a longitudinal migration or CG drift can develop and worsen undetected until effects become large.
fha.effCrew: Crew receives no annunciation of the loss and continues normal duties, taking no action regarding it (unaware case); the first cue is any resulting handling or CG anomaly, by which point the condition may be advanced.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect (flight crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The unaware, uncovered loss removes the crew's only cue and lets restraint degradation grow undetected, which tends to worsen severity; however the SDD does not define what fraction of restraint or which stations fall outside loop coverage, nor the resulting CG/structural effect, so I cannot derive a class from a stated aircraft effect. Missing: extent of monitoring-loop coverage gap and its restraint/CG consequence.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous restraint-loss annunciation with restraint intact
fha.effAc: Restraint is physically intact and the blade remains fully restrained; the aircraft's restraint state is unaffected. The failure is a false/spurious restraint-loss annunciation to the flight deck.
fha.effCrew: Crew is presented with a restraint condition that does not exist; because there is no in-flight adjustment of restraint, the erroneous alert can only prompt a diversion or precautionary decision and adds workload/distraction, with no corrective action possible.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect (flight crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft restraint is unaffected, so any effect is confined to crew workload/attention from a false alert during an otherwise normal flight; deriving whether this is Minor or No Safety Effect depends on the alert's priority/handling burden and any commanded procedure, which the SDD does not state. Missing: crew-alerting priority and required response for a restraint-loss annunciation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to annunciate genuine restraint-tension loss
fha.effAc: A genuine restraint-tension loss is present but not annunciated; the loss propagates as an unmonitored restraint degradation (as in the underlying SF-010 restraint condition) with the crew's warning cue removed, so any developing longitudinal migration or CG drift proceeds undetected.
fha.effCrew: Crew receives no alert of the genuine loss and continues normal duties taking no action; the failure removes the intended immediate-attention cue, so the crew cannot begin a diversion or precautionary response until an anomaly manifests.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect (flight crew only).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This monitoring failure is severe insofar as it strips the crew's cue from an underlying genuine restraint loss, but the aircraft effect is inherited from the restraint condition it masks (single-strap vs adjacent-station vs total), which is not fixed here, and the SDD gives no in-flight time-to-effect or CG margin to tie the missed annunciation to a specific aircraft outcome. Missing: the restraint condition being masked and the consequence window of undetected loss.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of restraint-tension monitoring coverage
fha.effAc: A subset of restraint straps is no longer instrumented; a genuine tension loss within the uncovered stations would not be annunciated. The blade is still restrained by the saddle geometry and remaining straps, but crew awareness of restraint state is incomplete.
fha.effCrew: Crew retains monitoring on the covered stations; no immediate action, but a latent restraint degradation in the uncovered coverage could progress unannounced.
fha.effPax: None; hold is unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is loss of monitoring COVERAGE, not loss of restraint. The aircraft-level consequence depends on whether an uncovered restraint failure would develop into a payload-shift condition (SF-010), which this function's definition does not establish. Cannot ground an aircraft effect severe enough to classify from the monitoring function alone — needs the restraint-loss outcome and exposure to be determined.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of restraint-tension condition awareness
fha.effAc: No annunciation of restraint tension across any station. The blade remains restrained by saddle geometry and straps, but the crew has no indication of a developing restraint condition; a two-adjacent-station restraint loss would no longer be annunciated as a condition requiring immediate attention.
fha.effCrew: Crew loses the restraint-status indication used to detect a developing restraint failure; they would continue normally, unaware of any restraint degradation.
fha.effPax: None; hold is unoccupied in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This function provides awareness only; loss of awareness is a latent-detection loss. Its aircraft-level severity turns on the consequence of an UNDETECTED restraint failure (payload shift affecting CG/controllability), which is the SF-010 restraint function, not this monitoring function. Cannot classify the aircraft effect from the awareness function alone — the underlying restraint-loss severity and its exposure must be established.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded visor motion during ground operation
fha.effAc: The nose visor moves without command during a ground operation. Because the door cannot be operated in flight and this condition is confined to ground operation, there is no in-flight aircraft effect; the hazard is to ground personnel and to the door/airframe structure during handling.
fha.effCrew: Ground/flight crew conducting the loading procedure face an uncommanded moving nose structure; the pressure interlock precludes unlock with the hold pressurised but does not address ground motion.
fha.effPax: None; hold is unoccupied and this is a ground condition.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Condition is confined to ground operation ("cannot be operated in flight"). Aircraft-level in-flight severity is not applicable; the harm is ground-personnel/structural injury during handling, which the §__.1309 aircraft-effect ladder as applied here does not directly classify from this function's definition. Severity requires the ground-safety/occupational effect and any take-off configuration consequence to be established.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded nose-visor actuation requiring backup drive
fha.effAc: Primary hydraulic (system A) visor actuation is degraded and the electric backup drive is required to open/close the visor. The door still opens and closes; no in-flight effect, as the door is not operated in flight. Turnaround may be extended.
fha.effCrew: Ground crew reverts to the electric backup drive to complete the loading operation; degraded actuation is annunciated/handled at the ground handling panel.
fha.effPax: None; hold is unoccupied and this is a ground condition.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — A degraded-but-available ground actuation using the designed backup drive produces no in-flight aircraft effect. The only aircraft-level consequence available from this function is dispatch/turnaround impact, which the SDD notes (no line maintenance at the strip) but does not resolve into a classifiable aircraft effect. Cannot ground a severity from the function definition without the dispatch/operational consequence being established.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of nose-visor open/close capability
fha.effAc: Neither the primary hydraulic drive nor the electric backup can open/close the visor. The blade cannot be loaded or unloaded; the aircraft is dispatchable only if already closed and configured. With no line maintenance at the strip, an unopenable visor at the destination prevents unloading. No in-flight aircraft effect, as the door is not operated in flight.
fha.effCrew: Ground crew cannot complete loading/unloading through the nose access; the operation is halted pending recovery.
fha.effPax: None; hold is unoccupied and this is a ground condition.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Total loss of open/close capability is a ground-operational/dispatch condition with no in-flight aircraft effect derivable from this function (the door forms the pressure boundary and load path when CLOSED — that integrity is SF-013 lock/closure territory, not open/close capability). The aircraft-level effect here is operational availability, which the §__.1309 ladder does not classify from this function alone. Severity requires the operational/dispatch consequence to be established.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Latent loss of lock engagement in flight with pressure boundary compromised (crew unaware; continue duties, take no action)
fha.effAc: Nose visor lock engagement is lost in flight while the flight-deck indication continues to show locked; the door is a pressure-boundary element and a single structural load path with no structural redundancy. Loss of lock engagement with the hold pressurised threatens loss of the pressure boundary and forward-fuselage load path, i.e. potential structural failure / door departure in flight.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware and take no action; false indication and latency defeat detection until physical departure or decompression.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants aft of flight deck.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Derived from the SDD-stated effects: the door is the pressure boundary and the forward-fuselage structural load path with no structural redundancy (single load path, treated as structure); undetected in-flight loss of lock engagement threatens loss of that load path/pressure boundary in cruise. Proposed Catastrophic for engineer confirmation; §25.1309 objective Extremely Improbable (1x10^-9/fh). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial lock engagement below full latch/pin complement (fewer than twelve latches / eight pins engaged)
fha.effAc: Fewer than the full complement of twelve latches and eight pins engage; door closure is achieved but at reduced margin in the pressure boundary and structural load path. Residual capability depends on how many of the redundant latches/pins remain and whether the reduced set still carries pressure and structural loads.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants aft of flight deck.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD provides twelve latches and eight pins but does not state the structural/pressure substantiation for a reduced latch/pin count, so the aircraft effect of a partial complement (whether the remaining set carries limit/ultimate and pressure loads) cannot be grounded to a severity. Requires structural analysis of the degraded lock configuration.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of door-closure locking capability (door cannot be locked)
fha.effAc: The nose visor cannot be locked; lock status is displayed on the flight deck and is included in the take-off configuration check. Door operation is a ground procedure and cannot be performed in flight, so an inability to lock is detected on the ground and prevents dispatch with a secured pressure boundary.
fha.effCrew: Crew has continuous flight-deck lock-status indication and the take-off configuration check; a not-locked state is annunciated and dispatch is prevented.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants aft of flight deck.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — With lock-status indication and the take-off configuration check functioning, an inability to lock is detected on the ground and dispatch is prevented, so the credible aircraft effect is an operational (no-dispatch) one; but the SDD does not state a residual in-flight aircraft effect for a detected inability to lock, so a §25.1309 severity cannot be grounded without confirming detection is credited and no dispatch is possible.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous over-pressurisation of the fuselage
fha.effAc: Pressurisation control commands an erroneous fuselage over-pressure. Positive and negative pressure relief valves protect the structure independently of the control system; the hold is designed to a low differential only, so the structure sees an over-pressure demand that the independent relief valves are provided to arrest. Residual aircraft effect (structural over-pressure vs. relief-limited) depends on relief-valve capacity relative to the erroneous demand.
fha.effCrew: Crew sees differential pressure and cabin altitude on the avionics; erroneous over-pressurisation is displayed, and the crew can select the manual pressurisation mode.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants aft of flight deck.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD states positive/negative relief valves protect the structure independently of the control system, which caps the credible structural over-pressure, but does not state the relief-valve capacity relative to the maximum erroneous over-pressure demand nor the resulting structural margin; without that the residual aircraft effect (bounded discomfort/no-effect vs. structural exceedance) cannot be grounded to a severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous under-pressurisation / uncommanded depressurisation of the fuselage
fha.effAc: Loss of pressure differential; fuselage exposed to ambient at cruise altitude up to FL260.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted, don quick-donning oxygen masks and initiate emergency descent to a safe altitude; increased workload during descent and diversion.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Rapid/uncommanded depressurisation at FL260 requires immediate crew oxygen and emergency descent; with crew action (masks + descent) the outcome is a demanding but survivable diversion, consistent with Hazardous. Confirm against the preliminary hold differential (≈8,800 m equivalent) and the time-to-useful-consciousness at FL260 before freezing. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Slow undetected loss of pressure differential developing below crew alerting thresholds
fha.effAc: Gradual rise in effective cabin/flight-deck altitude without annunciation; fuselage differential decays undetected.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties normally and take no action (unaware); insidious onset of hypoxia degrades crew performance and judgement before recognition.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An undetected, insidious loss of pressure to a two-crew flight deck risks hypoxic incapacitation of both crew before recognition, which can progress toward loss of the aircraft; classed Hazardous pending confirmation of the alerting-threshold coverage (SF-014 monitoring) and the maximum undetected cabin altitude achievable at FL260. If both crew can be incapacitated with no independent detection, revisit toward Catastrophic. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded pressurisation control on backup / single-outflow-valve operation
fha.effAc: Pressurisation maintained on reduced-capability backup mode (single outflow valve or pneumatic backup); reduced control margin, differential held but with degraded regulation.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to degraded mode; select backup configuration and monitor; possible altitude/route restriction, increased workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Function still performed at reduced capability with an available backup (single-valve sufficiency stated, plus pneumatic backup and independent relief); crew alerted and able to manage with increased workload and possible restriction — consistent with Major. Confirm the backup schedule maintains an acceptable cabin altitude at FL260. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of pressurisation control
fha.effAc: No active pressurisation control; differential governed only by independent mechanical relief; effective cabin altitude rises toward ambient at cruise level.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted, don oxygen masks and initiate descent to a safe altitude; workload elevated during descent and diversion.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of pressurisation control at FL260, with only mechanical relief remaining, forces crew oxygen use and an emergency descent/diversion — demanding but survivable with crew action, consistent with Hazardous. Confirm against the preliminary hold differential and the loss-of-both-controllers architecture before freezing. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous air temperature / flow delivered to flight deck or hold
fha.effAc: Erroneous conditioning output (temperature or flow) to the flight-deck and/or hold conditioning zone; delivered air differs from commanded.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8).
