SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground an aircraft-level effect on the crew from the provided function definition: the SDD states flight-deck and hold are separate conditioning zones but does not characterise the magnitude/rate of the erroneous temperature or flow, nor whether it reaches crew-hazard thresholds (e.g. incapacitating heat, smoke, or fume introduction). Missing: the erroneous-output envelope and its effect on the flight-deck occupants. Severity left empty pending that characterisation — not benign by default.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded conditioning and air distribution on single-pack operation
fha.effAc: One air-cycle pack lost; remaining pack supplies flight deck and hold on a reduced conditioning schedule. Pressurisation control unaffected (separate function).
fha.effCrew: Crew reconfigure to single-pack; reduced conditioning schedule applied. Increased workload; no immediate loss of control of the aircraft.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: SDD states single-pack operation is permitted with a reduced hold conditioning schedule, implying a degraded but continued-safe-flight condition consistent with Minor. Flight-deck thermal/comfort consequence and any envelope limitation on single pack are not quantified in the function definition — confirm before accepting. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of air conditioning and distribution to flight deck and hold
fha.effAc: Loss of conditioned-air supply and distribution; pressurisation control is a separate function but conditioned-air loss removes flight-deck and hold environmental control.
fha.effCrew: Loss of flight-deck conditioning; crew comfort/performance degradation over time. Effect depends on whether pressurisation is retained and on diversion time — not stated in the function definition.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft-level effect of total loss of conditioning cannot be classified from the provided function definition: the relationship to pressurisation retention, the crew-performance impact over diversion time, and any coupling to the crew-oxygen/pressurisation functions are not stated. Empty pending effects grounding.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Ice protection annunciated available while not protecting surfaces and inlets
fha.effAc: Undetected ice accretion on surfaces and/or engine inlets while crew believe protection is active; degradation of aerodynamic performance and/or engine inlet condition in the icing envelope.
fha.effCrew: Crew take no protective action because status is annunciated available; misleading indication defeats the crew's ability to recognise and mitigate accretion.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed Hazardous: misleading annunciation removes crew awareness of a genuine hazard (accretion) in the icing envelope, an undetected/uncorrected condition. Final class depends on the icing certification envelope, accretion rate and available margins — confirm against the icing basis before accepting. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent bleed demand from ice protection degrading source capacity when protection not required
fha.effAc: Uncommanded/unnecessary bleed demand to the ice protection system reduces pack capacity via the shared cross-bleed manifold; performance penalty applied when protection not required.
fha.effCrew: Crew workload to identify and isolate the spurious demand; degraded conditioning/performance consequence not quantified.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The function definition and SDD state IPS-in-use reduces pack capacity, but the aircraft-level severity of an INADVERTENT bleed demand (magnitude of capacity reduction, performance penalty, and any coupling to ECS/thrust) is not quantified in the provided material. Empty pending effects grounding.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced ice protection on some protected surfaces, inlets or probes
fha.effAc: Partial loss of protection: one or more surfaces/inlets/zones unprotected while others remain protected; localised accretion possible in the icing envelope. Lost electrical zone is annunciated.
fha.effCrew: Loss of a zone is annunciated; crew respond per procedure (exit icing / manual selection). Increased workload; residual protection retained on remaining zones.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Partial-loss severity depends on WHICH surface/inlet/probe loses protection and its criticality (e.g. engine inlet vs a stabiliser heater zone), and on the icing envelope — not resolvable at aircraft-function level from the provided definition without identifying the affected surface. Empty pending effects grounding.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Ice protection available in one operating mode only (partial loss — protection retained on a single power/bleed means)
fha.effAc: Reduced ice-protection margin; protection retained through the surviving means (bleed via cross-bleed manifold OR the electrically heated zones) but with no further redundancy for the remaining exposure to the icing envelope.
fha.effCrew: Crew annunciated of the lost mode/zone; assumed to avoid or exit icing conditions per procedure and monitor the remaining coverage.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive an aircraft-level severity from the function definition alone: the SDD states ice protection is available from either bleed side and lost electrical zones are annunciated, but it does not state the aircraft effect of remaining in the icing envelope on single-mode protection. Missing: icing-envelope exposure assumption and the residual-protection adequacy against that envelope. Engineer to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of surface and inlet ice protection (no protection available by any means)
fha.effAc: With flight continued in the icing envelope, unchecked accretion on wing leading edges, engine inlet cowls and stabiliser surfaces degrades lift, increases drag and threatens engine inlet integrity and control authority; potential loss of control if the envelope is not exited.
fha.effCrew: Crew annunciated of the loss; assumed to exit icing conditions immediately and divert; workload elevated during the escape.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect direction is grounded (protection removed for wings, inlets, probes/stabiliser per §5.10), but the aircraft-level severity depends on the certification icing envelope and how quickly the aircraft can exit it — neither is stated in the SDD. Missing: icing-envelope exposure, accretion-rate/escape-time basis. Engineer to classify (candidate Hazardous/Catastrophic pending exposure data).. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous icing detection state — false indication (icing annunciated with none present) or missed indication (icing present, not annunciated)
fha.effAc: Missed indication in automatic mode leaves protection off while ice accretes on unprotected surfaces/inlets/probes, degrading performance and air data; false indication commands protection on unnecessarily, imposing a bleed/performance penalty. Detection is advisory and manual selection remains available.
fha.effCrew: Crew may operate on erroneous icing status; on missed detection they take no protective action until other cues appear, then select protection manually; on false detection they carry an unwarranted penalty.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD states detection is advisory with manual selection always available, which bounds the effect, but the aircraft-level consequence of a MISSED indication before manual selection (accretion on unprotected surfaces and probes) is not quantified. Missing: icing-envelope exposure and the time to independent crew recognition. Engineer to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Probe protection annunciated healthy while not actually protecting (erroneous healthy state, crew aware of the indication only)
fha.effAc: Unprotected probes/static ports may ice in the icing envelope, corrupting air data (airspeed, altitude, angle of attack) fed to the avionics while indication shows protection healthy; erroneous air data can propagate to displays and flight envelope protection.
fha.effCrew: Crew trusts a healthy annunciation and takes no protective action; misleading air data may not be recognised until cross-comparison flags a discrepancy.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect chain (unprotected iced probes → corrupted air data) is grounded in §5.10/§5.11, but the aircraft-level severity of the resulting erroneous air data is not stated in the SDD and depends on avionics voting/comparator coverage and crew recognition. Missing: air-data monitoring/detection coverage and icing-envelope exposure. Engineer to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of probe protection developing below detection thresholds (latent, crew unaware — continue duties normally, no action taken)
fha.effAc: Latent probe-protection loss below the monitoring threshold allows gradual probe/port icing in the icing envelope, producing slowly corrupting air data with no annunciation; erroneous air data may reach displays and envelope protection before any cue appears.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware; continue normal duties and take no protective action; recognition depends on eventual air-data discrepancy or accretion cues, not on the protection indication.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Latency is grounded (loss developing below detection thresholds, monitored individually per §5.10), but the aircraft-level severity of undetected corrupted air data is not stated in the SDD and depends on air-data comparator coverage and icing exposure. Missing: air-data monitoring coverage and icing-envelope exposure. Engineer to classify — latency typically drives severity up relative to the aware case.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous icing detection state (false-clear or false-detect) presented to crew and automatic activation logic
fha.effAc: In icing conditions a false-clear state suppresses automatic ice protection and denies the crew the cue to select it manually; ice accretes on unprotected/underprotected surfaces, inlets and probes, degrading lift/drag, control margins and engine/probe integrity while the crew believes conditions are clear.
fha.effCrew: Crew take no protective action because the detection state is believed valid; no annunciation prompts reassessment.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects rest on an operational assumption (flight within the certified icing envelope) that the function definitions do not themselves establish, and the SDD does not state the aircraft-level outcome of undetected ice accretion on this configuration. Severity left empty pending confirmation of the icing exposure and the accretion consequence before deriving a class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of icing detection with probe/port protection retained
fha.effAc: Automatic activation cue is lost but heated probes, static ports and windshields remain protected; crew retain the option to select ice protection manually at any time, so surface/inlet protection can still be commanded on detection of icing by other means.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise icing without the detection advisory and select protection manually; increased monitoring workload but a manual reversion exists.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD establishes manual selection is available at any time and probe protection is retained, but the function definitions do not state the aircraft-level effect of delayed/missed manual activation in the icing envelope. Severity left empty pending the icing-exposure consequence rather than assigning a benign class by default.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of protection on some monitored probes/ports (partial loss of probe/port heating)
fha.effAc: Some probes/static ports lose heating while others remain protected; affected sensors may ice, producing unreliable air-data inputs from the affected channels while redundant protected sensors remain available; individual monitoring of heated elements supports detection of the lost channel.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to the lost heated element(s) via individual monitoring; must manage possible unreliable air-data from the affected channel and select alternate sources.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD confirms probes/ports are heated and monitored individually, but the function definitions do not state the aircraft-level effect of an iced sensor channel on air-data integrity for this configuration. Severity left empty pending that air-data consequence rather than presuming a class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of probe protection and icing detection
fha.effAc: With all probe/port heating and both ice detectors lost, flight in the icing envelope allows ice accretion on probes, static ports, surfaces and inlets with no detection cue and no protection; air-data and control/engine integrity degrade progressively and the crew has neither an advisory nor a protective means.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of icing onset (detection lost) and unable to protect probes; must diagnose from secondary symptoms and exit the icing envelope.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The concurrent loss of protection and detection is grounded in the function, but the aircraft-level severity depends on the icing-envelope exposure and the accretion/air-data consequence, which the provided functions and SDD do not quantify. Severity left empty rather than assigning a class on an assumed exposure.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous flight/navigation information presented as valid on the primary displays
fha.effAc: Erroneous attitude, air-data or navigation information presented as valid can lead the crew or autopilot to fly the aircraft toward an unsafe state (loss of control, controlled flight toward terrain, unsafe configuration/speed) when the error is undetected and acted upon as truth.
fha.effCrew: Crew act on misleading information believed valid; excessive workload to detect and cross-check against the independent standby instrument before an unrecoverable state develops.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Misleading primary flight/navigation information presented as valid and acted upon can produce a loss-of-control or CFIT outcome — the effect drives Catastrophic (↔ Extremely Improbable, 1e-9/fh). The independent standby instrument that shares no supply/sensor/processing is a design mitigation, not an FHA input; confirm before finalising the class. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Display of flight/navigation information annunciated invalid (crew aware; primary display data flagged, standby retained)
fha.effAc: Primary flight/navigation display data annunciated invalid; aircraft continues to be flown on retained standby attitude, airspeed and altitude on the DC essential bus.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware via annunciation; revert to independent standby instrument and any valid alternate formats; increased workload and cross-check burden.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Annunciated invalidity with the independent standby (shares no supply, sensor or processing per SDD §5.11.3) retained leaves the crew aware with a usable alternate; proposed Major from increased workload/reduced margin — confirm against the worst applicable phase and standby sufficiency. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous flight/navigation information presented as valid (crew unaware; no annunciation, cross-check defeated)
fha.effAc: Erroneous primary flight/navigation information presented as valid with no annunciation; crew act on false data, potentially commanding the aircraft outside a safe state and toward loss of control.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware and continue normal duties acting on the erroneous data; the standby exists but is not consulted absent an annunciation to prompt reversion.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected, unannunciated erroneous primary flight/navigation data acted upon can lead to loss of control with no crew cue to revert to standby; proposed Catastrophic ↔ Extremely Improbable (1e-9/fh). Confirm the unaware assumption and whether a common erroneous state can defeat the three-ADIRU cross-monitor. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of a flight/navigation parameter (parameter absent from the presentation without annunciation)
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground an aircraft/crew effect: the provided function definition does not identify WHICH parameter is lost, and severity depends entirely on that parameter's criticality and whether its absence is itself a detectable cue. Engineer to specify the parameter set (e.g. attitude vs a secondary display value) before an effect and severity can be derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of primary display with standby information retained (crew aware)
fha.effAc: Primary flight/navigation display lost; aircraft flown on the retained independent standby attitude, airspeed and altitude and any available reversionary display formats.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware of the loss; select reversionary display and/or revert to the standby instrument; increased workload, reduced information redundancy for the remainder of the flight.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of primary display with the independent standby retained and manual reversionary selection available leaves a flyable, aware degraded state; proposed Major from significant workload increase and loss of redundancy — confirm against approach/landing as the worst applicable phase. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of some flight/navigation parameters or formats (crew aware; partial degradation of the presentation)
fha.effAc: A subset of flight/navigation parameters or display formats unavailable; core presentation and standby remain; aircraft flown with reduced information set.
fha.effCrew: Crew aware of missing parameters/formats; reconfigure displays and use remaining formats and standby; modest workload increase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity cannot be derived without knowing WHICH parameters/formats are within the lost subset — loss of a secondary format and loss of a primary parameter classify very differently. Engineer to bound the parameter/format set; effEffAc/effCrew stated qualitatively but severity left blank rather than guessed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of flight and navigation information display
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: No primary flight or navigation information presented on the four display units and two head-up displays; aircraft controllable but crew reduced to the independent integrated standby instrument (attitude, airspeed, altitude) which shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primary displays.
fha.effCrew: Crew loses primary attitude, air data and navigation picture; workload rises sharply, flown on standby attitude/airspeed/altitude only for the remainder of the flight including approach and landing in the low flight levels under IFR.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of primary flight/nav display leaves only the standby instrument for IFR flight and landing; large increase in crew workload and a serious degradation of safety margins, which is the Hazardous case. Proposed pending confirmation that standby capability is sufficient to avoid a Catastrophic outcome across all applicable phases. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: False or spurious crew alerts presented
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Aircraft systems function normally; no actual failure exists but the alerting system presents false or spurious alerts.
fha.effCrew: Crew distraction and increased workload responding to or diagnosing alerts that do not correspond to a real condition; risk of unnecessary crew action and erosion of trust in genuine alerting.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: False/spurious alerting with no underlying failure produces crew distraction and increased workload but does not itself degrade a flight function; proposed Major on the workload/distraction effect pending confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Missed or suppressed crew alert for an active condition
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: A genuine active system condition exists but is not annunciated; the aircraft state depends on which underlying condition is masked, which the alerting function definition alone does not bound.
fha.effCrew: Crew is not informed of a real, active failure and continues normal duties taking no corrective action; the associated procedure is not triggered.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity cannot be grounded from the aircraft-level alerting function alone: the effect on the aircraft depends entirely on WHICH underlying condition is left unannunciated (a masked Catastrophic condition versus a masked Minor one). Classification requires the specific set of alerts the alerting function is required to present and their own severities — not supplied at aircraft-function level. Left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Misprioritised crew alert list
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Alerts are presented but in an incorrect priority order within the consolidated crew alert list; the correct alerts are present but a lower-priority item may mask or delay crew attention to a higher-priority one.
fha.effCrew: Crew may act on a less urgent alert first or take longer to identify the most significant condition, increasing workload and delaying the correct procedure.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Misprioritisation delays but does not prevent crew awareness of an active condition; proposed Major on the delayed-response and workload effect. Confirm — could rise if a delayed higher-priority response can itself lead to a Hazardous outcome for time-critical conditions. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of alerting on one processing channel
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: One of the two independent alerting processing channels is lost; the second channel continues to consolidate and present the prioritised crew alert list, so alerting capability is retained with reduced redundancy.
fha.effCrew: No immediate loss of alerting function to the crew; loss of the redundant channel is annunciated and the crew retains full alerting on the remaining channel.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With two independent processing channels, loss of one leaves alerting intact on the other; effect is a redundancy reduction with a slight increase in crew awareness of degraded state. Proposed Minor pending confirmation of the dual-channel independence claim. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of alert prioritisation or associated procedures within crew alerting
fha.effAc: Alerts may still be presented but without correct prioritisation or associated corrective procedure; a lower-priority alert can mask or delay recognition of a higher-priority condition, degrading the crew's ability to identify and respond to the driving failure.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload and diagnostic burden; potential for delayed or incorrect response where the prioritised alert list or its linked procedure is the intended aid.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; no direct effect on occupants.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground an aircraft-level severity from the definition alone: the effect depends on which alerts lose prioritisation and whether the driving condition is otherwise annunciated — the SDD states the alerting 'consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures' but does not establish the worst-case consequence of losing prioritisation. Left empty pending crew-response and worst-alert analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of crew alerting
fha.effAc: No consolidated fire, overheat, system-status or configuration alerting is presented to the crew; failures across all systems that rely on the alerting list go un-annunciated, so the crew is not prompted to a failed state and cannot invoke the associated procedure.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in crew workload and reliance on manual cross-checking of individual displays; loss of the primary means by which the crew learns what has failed and what to do, degrading timely response across multiple systems.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; no direct effect on occupants.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Total loss of the single prioritised alert list removes the crew's primary means of detecting and responding to failures fleet-wide, materially reducing safety margins and increasing crew workload to the point that the crew cannot be relied upon to perform their tasks accurately or completely — consistent with the Hazardous definition. The alerting is 'driven by two independent processing channels', so complete loss is a two-channel condition; confirm the dual-channel independence and the residual standby indications before fixing the class. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: False fire or overheat warning with no fire present
fha.effAc: A spurious fire/overheat warning is presented; if actioned per procedure it can lead to unnecessary engine or APU shutdown and agent discharge, reducing available thrust/redundancy for the remainder of the flight and, on an outboard engine, imposing the asymmetric-thrust directional-control case.
fha.effCrew: Crew responds to a genuine-appearing warning with the fire drill (fire handle, shutdown, discharge); increased workload and a decision under time pressure on a false premise.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; no direct effect on occupants.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground severity from the function definition alone: the aircraft-level consequence turns on whether an unnecessary engine shutdown (and its asymmetric-thrust case at the 28 m outboard moment arm) is credibly commanded on a single false warning, versus crew cross-check limiting it. The SDD supports the four-engine/outboard-moment-arm concern but does not establish the false-warning outcome. Left empty pending analysis of the crew action and dual-loop AND logic.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Missed fire or overheat with condition present
fha.effAc: A genuine fire or overheat in a monitored zone (engine nacelle, APU compartment, bleed duct run, main gear bay, or hold smoke) is not annunciated; an undetected fire can propagate uncontained before the crew can invoke suppression, threatening structure, control runs and systems in the affected zone.
fha.effCrew: Crew receives no warning and takes no fire action; the failure is unrevealed until secondary effects appear, by which point the event may be beyond the crew's ability to control.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; no direct effect on occupants.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Failure to detect a fire that is actually present removes the crew's opportunity to extinguish it before it propagates in a fire zone (engine/APU/bleed/gear) or, in the hold, before an undetected fire develops with no fitted suppression; an undetected in-flight fire is a recognised catastrophic risk. Confirm against the dual-loop detection architecture — a missed condition requires loss of both separately routed loops (or degraded single-loop coverage), which bears on likelihood, not on this severity classification. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of detection in some monitored zones
fha.effAc: Fire/overheat detection is lost in one or more monitored zones while retained in others; a fire or overheat originating in an unmonitored zone would go un-annunciated, while the remaining zones stay protected — a partial reduction of the detection coverage on which the fire-protection concept depends.
fha.effCrew: Reduced detection coverage may be annunciated as a degraded-detection state; crew retains warning for the still-covered zones but has no warning for the affected zone.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; no direct effect on occupants.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground an aircraft-level severity from the definition alone: consequence depends on WHICH zones lose coverage (a fire zone such as a nacelle/APU versus overheat-only detection on a bleed run) and whether the loss is annunciated to the crew — the SDD lists distinct monitored zones with dual-loop-to-single-loop degradation but does not fix the worst-case partial loss. Left empty pending zone-by-zone effects analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Fire and overheat detection degraded to single-channel (single-loop) logic in a monitored zone
fha.effAc: Detection in the affected zone reverts from dual-loop AND warning logic to single-loop logic; a genuine fire/overheat remains detectable via the surviving loop but the confirmation/nuisance-rejection margin is reduced.
fha.effCrew: Loss annunciated; crew retains fire warning on the surviving loop and applies normal procedures.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold in flight; no direct effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive an aircraft-level severity from the stated effects: single-loop logic is a designed degraded mode that retains detection, so the consequence depends on the probability of the surviving loop failing before repair and on which zone is affected — neither stated. Needs engineering judgement / exposure data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire and overheat detection
fha.effAc: No detection of fire or overheat in the engine nacelles, APU compartment, bleed-duct runs or main gear bays; a developing fire could progress undetected in a fire zone (high-energy, flammable fluid) with no warning to trigger isolation or extinguishing.
fha.effCrew: Crew receives no fire/overheat warning and cannot initiate the fire handles or agent discharge in response to a real fire; unable to isolate a burning engine or bleed leak in time.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold in flight; no direct effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Derived from effects: total loss of detection removes the trigger for isolating and extinguishing an undetected fire in a nacelle/APU/bleed/gear fire zone where flammable fluid and high energy are present; an uncontained undetected fire is potentially catastrophic. PROPOSED for confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent extinguishing-agent discharge on (erroneous) crew command
fha.effAc: Agent bottle discharged into a nacelle with no fire present, consuming a finite extinguishing resource; with two bottles per engine pair cross-plumbed, a spurious discharge reduces the agent available for a subsequent genuine fire on that pair.
fha.effCrew: Crew loses one shot of extinguishing capability for the affected engine pair; must manage the aircraft with reduced fire-suppression reserve.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold in flight; no direct effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Derived from effects: no immediate hazard from discharging inert agent into a fire-free nacelle, but it depletes a limited reserve (two bottles per pair) and degrades the response to a later genuine fire — a significant reduction in safety margin. PROPOSED for confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Extinguishing-agent discharge into the wrong protected zone
fha.effAc: Agent delivered to a nacelle other than the one requiring suppression; the actual fire zone receives no agent while a finite reserve is consumed into the wrong nacelle of the pair.
fha.effCrew: Crew commands discharge expecting suppression of the affected zone but the fire zone remains unprotected; may be unaware the agent went to the wrong nacelle.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold in flight; no direct effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive an aircraft-level severity from the stated effects alone: the outcome depends on whether a genuine fire is present in the mis-served pair and whether the second (cross-plumbed) bottle can still reach the true fire zone — the SDD's cross-plumbing means either bottle can reach either nacelle, so the mis-routing mechanism and its residual capability are not resolved. Needs architecture clarification.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Extinguishing agent unavailable on demand with no prior indication (latent loss of extinguishing capability)
fha.effAc: On a genuine fire the commanded agent discharge does not occur and no prior annunciation warned the crew; the fire in a nacelle/APU fire zone (flammable fluid, high energy) cannot be extinguished by the aircraft system.
fha.effCrew: Crew initiates the fire handle expecting suppression, receives no discharge, and has no remaining aircraft means to extinguish a nacelle/APU fire; left to shutdown/isolation and diversion only.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold in flight; no direct effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Derived from effects: latent unavailability of extinguishing on demand, combined with a genuine fire in a fire zone with flammable fluid and high energy, leaves no means to extinguish an escalating fire — potentially catastrophic. Latency (no prior indication) removes any pre-flight or in-flight opportunity to detect it. PROPOSED for confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced fire extinguishing agent availability
fha.effAc: Fewer agent shots available than the two-bottles-per-engine-pair provision; a fire re-flash or a second engine event may not be extinguishable, but at least one discharge into an affected nacelle remains available.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain fire-handle discharge capability with reduced margin; degraded state annunciated via alerting.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold in flight; no direct effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a class: the SDD states two bottles per engine pair cross-plumbed but does not quantify how many shots 'reduced' leaves, nor the consequence of an unextinguished nacelle fire on continued safe flight. Effect-to-severity chain not closeable from provided material.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of fire extinguishing to one protected zone
fha.effAc: One nacelle or the APU compartment cannot receive extinguishing agent; a fire in that zone must be managed by shutdown/fuel isolation alone, without agent knock-down, risking uncontrolled propagation from a fire zone containing flammable fluid and high energy.
fha.effCrew: Crew execute fire-handle shutdown and fuel isolation for the affected zone but cannot discharge agent into it; condition annunciated.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold in flight; no direct effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot close severity: consequence of an unextinguishable fire in a specific fire zone (nacelle vs APU) on continued safe flight and landing is not stated in the SDD, which declines to classify. Whether shutdown/isolation alone bounds the fire is the analysis result, not given.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire extinguishing capability
fha.effAc: No means to extinguish or suppress a fire in any protected zone (engine nacelles, APU); a fire once detected can only be managed by engine shutdown and fuel isolation, with no agent available to arrest it in a flammable-fluid, high-energy fire zone.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain detection and shutdown/isolation actions but have no extinguishing means; condition annunciated.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold in flight; no direct effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect stated but severity not classifiable from provided inputs: whether an unextinguishable in-flight fire is Hazardous or Catastrophic depends on the fire-scenario progression and continued-safe-flight analysis the SDD explicitly does not perform. Do not assume a class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous crew oxygen delivery
fha.effAc: Aircraft unaffected directly; hazard is to crew supply during a loss-of-pressurisation, smoke or fume event.
fha.effCrew: Crew may receive oxygen that is contaminated, interrupted, or at incorrect flow during the very events (depressurisation, smoke/fume) for which the system exists, with potential for crew impairment or incapacitation at low differential / high hold-altitude equivalent operation.
fha.effPax: No passenger oxygen fitted; hold unoccupied in flight; no direct effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a class: 'erroneous delivery' is not defined in the provided material (contaminated vs interrupted vs excess/insufficient flow), so the crew-incapacitation effect and its coincidence with a depressurisation event cannot be closed to a severity. Two independent regulators per mask noted but the failure mode is unspecified.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced crew oxygen supply duration
fha.effAc: Oxygen supply endurance below the sized diversion time associated with the maximum operating altitude; aircraft may not be able to complete a diversion with protected crew if a loss-of-pressurisation or smoke/fume event occurs.
fha.effCrew: Crew oxygen available but for less than the required diversion duration at reduced reserve; low-pressure alerting and dispatch pressure check give awareness, but a prolonged descent/diversion may exhaust supply.
fha.effPax: No passenger oxygen fitted; hold unoccupied in flight; no direct effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot close severity: the SDD states sizing for four occupants for the diversion time with reserve but does not state the consequence of falling below that duration during an actual depressurisation/smoke event, nor the exposure. Effect-to-severity chain not derivable from provided material.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of oxygen to one mask station
fha.effCrew: One of four mask stations without oxygen; remaining three stations available to the nominal two-crew (max four) complement for the diversion. Affected crew member must relocate to a functioning station or share.
fha.effPax: None — hold is unoccupied in flight, no passenger oxygen fitted.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Regulators are independent per mask and the system serves four stations for a nominal two-crew complement; loss of one station still leaves protection for the crew, with a workload increase to relocate. Proposed for engineer confirmation; confirm crew complement and whether a single-station loss during depressurisation degrades crew capability beyond a slight increase in workload. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded oxygen delivery below alerting threshold
fha.effCrew: Reduced oxygen supply capability (duration/flow) not annunciated; crew continue normally, unaware. On a subsequent depressurisation or smoke/fume event the available protection is less than assumed, potentially insufficient for the diversion time from FL260.
fha.effPax: None — hold is unoccupied in flight, no passenger oxygen fitted.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Latent (crew-unaware) degradation whose consequence is only realised if it coincides with a demand event; severity depends on how far below the required duration/flow the delivery falls and the probability of coincidence with a depressurisation/smoke event — neither is stated in the SDD. Cannot derive a defensible class from the provided material; left empty pending that data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of crew breathing oxygen supply
fha.effCrew: No breathing oxygen available to any crew station. In the event of a depressurisation at up to FL260, or a smoke/fume event, the crew have no protected air supply for the descent and diversion the system exists to cover; risk of incapacitation.
fha.effPax: None — hold is unoccupied in flight, no passenger oxygen fitted.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss removes crew protection for the depressurisation/smoke/fume events the system is provided for; the effect is realised only when such an event occurs, so this classifies the coincident condition. Proposed Hazardous for engineer confirmation — a total-loss coincident with depressurisation at FL260 could threaten crew capability; whether it reaches Catastrophic depends on cabin-altitude time-of-useful-consciousness at FL260 and available emergency descent, which are not quantified in the SDD. — engineer to confirm.

assumptions.text: The aircraft-level function set is derived from system purposes because the SDD enumerates no functions.
assumptions.rationale: Appendix A explicitly states the document does not list aircraft-level functions, forcing derivation from each system's stated purpose.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the intended function taxonomy differs, the top-function names and their sub-function groupings change, altering every downstream AFHA-to-SFHA trace.

citations.quote: It does not tell you what the aircraft-level functions are.

assumptions.text: Fuel, hydraulic power, electrical power and wiring interconnection are resources and are excluded as functions.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD inventory tags FUE/HYD/EPS/EWS as Resource type; the modeling rule bars authoring resources as functions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any resource must be modelled as a function, an additional top-level function and its FHA row would be required.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion of FUE/HYD/EPS/EWS from the function list.

citations.quote: Four are treated as resources — they exist to supply other systems

assumptions.text: The nose door structure and hold floor hard points are structure and are not authored as functions.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD explicitly treats the door as a single load-path structure and states no redundancy in the hard points; structural integrity is not a functional-FHA item.
assumptions.ifWrong: If treated functionally, additional structural-support functions would appear, but they belong to structural analysis and PRA instead.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion of nose-door structural load path and hold hard points from the function list.

citations.quote: the door is a single load path and is treated as structure

assumptions.text: Reverse thrust is grouped under the propulsion 'Provide thrust' top function rather than under ground deceleration.
assumptions.rationale: Reversers are a propulsion-system behaviour but contribute to ground deceleration; the SDD does not fix which aircraft function owns it, forcing an allocation choice.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reverse thrust belongs under ground deceleration, the sub-function moves and its up-trace target changes.
assumptions.usedFor: add_function 'Provide reverse thrust on ground' placement.

citations.quote: Thrust reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only.

assumptions.text: The awareness split for the primary flight-control axes cannot be fully grounded until effects and detection means are established, so Unaware rows carry only the below-threshold variants and the indication/mitigation fields are left empty.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes 'asymmetry and jam discretes' but does not state detection thresholds or which malfunction variants annunciate, so the crew-Aware vs Unaware boundary per condition is not groundable here.
assumptions.ifWrong: If some erroneous/uncommanded variants are in fact always annunciated, the corresponding Unaware rows should be removed; if none are, the Aware indication fields need filling.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003/SF-004/SF-005 Aware and Unaware rows, and their empty indication fields

citations.quote: asymmetry and jam discretes
